title: Perfect acceptance forces the final proof bit
statement: Let $m$ be a natural number, let $w$ be a Boolean word of length $m+2$, and let $p$ be a Boolean proof word of length $m+1$. If the odd-weight partial-sum PCPP system accepts $(w,p)$ with probability $1$, then the last bit of $p$ is true.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean proof word of length $m+1$
The system's acceptance probability on these words equals $1$
